venue.name: Mount Arrowsmith Biosphere Region
venue.description: The Mount Arrowsmith Biosphere Region is one of 19 UNESCO designated biosphere regions in Canada and a community based organisation working across Parksville, Qualicum Beach and the surrounding area. It is not a site you take a group to see. Its offering to schools is a free youth programme of hands on workshops that staff bring to the classroom, two of which then move outdoors to a local beach or a forest that the class travels to itself. The organisation also runs an education centre at 124 West Second Avenue in Qualicum Beach, but the site describes no visit or activity for children's groups there.
venue.address: ts'xwelikwshenawtxw, 124 West Second Avenue, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1S9
restrictions: The workshops are available to schools and organizations within the Mount Arrowsmith Biosphere Region.
Each class is responsible for its own transportation to the outdoor destinations.
venue.hours_notes: The MABR Education Centre in Qualicum Beach does not currently have fixed business hours. Visitors are encouraged to stop by Wednesday through Friday, 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Staff are generally on site Monday to Friday, and they recommend calling ahead to confirm.

programs.name: Coastal Ecosystems Workshop
programs.description: A workshop on the connection between people and aquatic ecosystems, covering local watersheds, water pollution, biodiversity, marine food webs and human impacts in the biosphere region. It is made up of a presentation, classroom activities on marine food webs and water pollution, and a beach seine at a local beach or at the Deep Bay Marine Field Station. The site says the whole thing runs about 4 to 5 hours, and that the materials can be modified to suit the class's availability. It is free, but the class arranges and pays for its own travel to the beach.
programs.what_children_do: Sit for a presentation and then work at tables on marine food webs and water pollution. The rest of the day is spent on a beach, pulling a seine net through the shallows and looking at what comes up in it.
programs.our_note: The workshop costs nothing, but getting the class to the beach is on you and that is the part that will decide whether you can run it. Block off most of a school day, because four to five hours with a beach in the middle is a long stretch for younger children. Ask which beach they have in mind before you book the bus.
programs.practical_summary: Half of this is indoors in your own classroom and half is on an open beach, so plan for weather, footwear and a change of clothes. Nothing is published about washrooms at the beach, lunch, or how many adults have to come, so ask when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: Each class is responsible for its own transportation to the destinations.
programs.evidence: The program is available to any school or organization within the MABR cost-free.

programs.name: Terrestrial Ecosystems Workshop
programs.description: A workshop on local biodiversity, ecosystem services and environmental sustainability, covering flora and fauna, food chains, connectivity and human impacts in the biosphere region. It is made up of a classroom presentation, classroom activities on soil types and food webs, and then a field trip to a forested area chosen by the organisers where the class does a scavenger hunt for local plant species. The site says the whole thing runs about 4 to 5 hours. It is free, but the class arranges and pays for its own travel to the forest.
programs.what_children_do: Listen to a presentation, then handle soil types and build food webs at tables. Outdoors they walk in a forest and hunt for named local plants on a scavenger list.
programs.our_note: The forest site is picked by them, not by you, so ask where it is and how far the walk in is before you agree a date. Four to five hours including a woodland scavenger hunt suits a class that is already used to walking. The workshop itself is free but the bus is not.
programs.practical_summary: Part classroom, part forest, so boots and layers matter and the outdoor half has no shelter mentioned. Washrooms at the forest site, lunch arrangements and how many adults have to come are all unstated, so ask when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: Each class is responsible for its own transportation to the destinations.
programs.evidence: The program is available to any school or organization within the MABR cost-free.

programs.name: Sustainable Development Workshop
programs.description: A classroom workshop on the three pillars of sustainability, ecological footprints, environmental responsibility and building sustainable local cities. It is a presentation followed by interactive activities on ecological footprints and on designing a sustainable city. The site says it runs about 1.5 to 2 hours. Unlike the coastal and terrestrial workshops it stays indoors, so there is no travel involved.
programs.what_children_do: Watch a presentation, then work in groups on their own ecological footprint and design a sustainable city together.
programs.our_note: This is the one that needs no bus and no boots, which makes it the easiest of the three to actually get approved. Under two hours in your own room also makes it the safest bet for a younger or a restless class.
programs.practical_summary: It happens in your own classroom, so washrooms, lunch and wet weather are all your own arrangements. What is not published is which grades it suits or how large a class they will take, so ask when you book.
programs.evidence: These workshops are best suited for elementary school students.

programs.name: Sustainable Development Goals Workshop
programs.description: A classroom workshop listed by the organisers under high school workshops. It covers the 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, how people can contribute to them and why sustainability matters. It is a presentation followed by an activity in the style of Dragon's Den in which students pitch sustainable ideas for their own community. The site says it runs about 1.5 hours and can be shortened or lengthened to fit the class's timetable.
programs.what_children_do: Sit through a presentation on the 17 goals, then work up a sustainable idea for their own town and pitch it to the room.
programs.our_note: This one is written for high school, so it is the wrong fit for a daycare or the early primary years. It stays in your own classroom and needs nothing more than desks and about an hour and a half.
programs.practical_summary: Everything happens in your own room, so the practical side is entirely yours. The site does not say which grades it is pitched at beyond calling it a high school workshop, so ask when you book.
programs.evidence: Total workshop duration is approximately 1.5 hours, but can be modified to your classrooms availability.

images.alt: A large group of people gathered on the steps and lawn of a yellow single storey house with a covered porch and a white picket fence.
People standing on the pavement and around a low stone planter in front of a yellow house with a covered porch, seen from the street.
Children and adults stand barefoot in shallow water on a wide sandy beach, several of them holding a long net between them, with an orange bucket on the sand.
Four children sit around a table working with markers on a large printed ocean scene while an adult leans in to help, with display banners behind them.

gaps: There is nowhere here to take a group. The biosphere region is an area of land and water, not a site, and the education centre in Qualicum Beach has no visit, tour or activity for children's groups described anywhere on the site. What they offer instead is a free workshop that comes to your classroom.

No age or grade range is published for any of the workshops. Three are grouped under the heading elementary school workshops and one under high school workshops, and the copy says the elementary ones are best suited for elementary school students, but no grades or ages are given. Worth settling in the first email.

Two of the workshops give their length as approximately 4 to 5 hours and one as approximately 1.5 to 2 hours. A range cannot be recorded as a single number, so the lengths sit in the descriptions rather than in the timing on the card.
No group size is published, either a maximum or a minimum, and no notice period is given for booking.

The outdoor destinations are not named. The coastal workshop says a local beach or the Deep Bay Marine Field Station, and the terrestrial one says a predetermined forested area. Which site, and how far it is from the school, has to be asked.
Nothing is published about washrooms at the outdoor sites, about a lunch stop, about what happens in bad weather, or about how many adults have to come.
The workshops are open to schools and organizations within the biosphere region. Whether a daycare counts as an organization for this, and whether under fives are welcome, is not stated.

The booking address published for the workshops is a Vancouver Island University address for the research and community engagement coordinator, not an address on the biosphere region's own domain. The general enquiry address on their contact page is used as the fallback.

The organisation also lists ten Amazing Places, which are provincial, regional and municipal parks such as MacMillan Provincial Park and Rathtrevor Beach. Those are public parks run by others, not places the biosphere region admits groups to, so they are not recorded as programs here.

A NatureKids club runs in Qualicum Beach in partnership with NatureKids BC, for children five and older, on the fourth Wednesday of the month. It is a family membership club joined through NatureKids BC rather than a group booking, so it is not recorded as a program.

Printable Biosphere Booklets for grades 1 to 7 and at home activity sheets are published for teachers to download. They are classroom resources rather than a bookable offering, so they are not recorded as programs.
The Open Graph image on every page is the organisation's round logo rather than a photograph, so it was skipped and the picture used is the banner photograph on the home page.

The two workshop photographs sit in a shared gallery at the foot of the workshops page rather than beside a particular workshop. The beach seine photograph is tied to the coastal workshop here because that is the only workshop the page describes a beach seine in. Their alt text on the site is the camera's file name, so plain descriptions were written for them.

No coordinates are published anywhere on the site, so the point on the map was worked out from the education centre street address. It marks the office in Qualicum Beach, not the biosphere region, which covers a large area of central Vancouver Island and has no single centre a group could be sent to.
